title: Groups, inverses, and commutativity
section: Part B: Abstract Algebra ▷ Binary Structures and the Definition of a Group
terms: group; inverse; Abelian group; commutative operation; finite group; infinite group; group order; cancellation law.

exposition.text:
A group is a monoid in which every element has a two-sided inverse. It is Abelian if ab = ba for
every pair of elements. Its order |G| is its cardinality, finite or infinite. In a group, ax = b and
−1 −1
ya = b have the unique solutions x = a b and y = ba .
−1 −1 −1
Inverses reverse order: (ab) = b a . Cancellation is valid, but factors cannot be commuted
2 2 2
without a hypothesis. For example, (ab) = a b for every a, b holds exactly when the group
is Abelian. The identity has order one even though the symbol used for it may be 0, 1, or an
identity matrix.
Standard infinite Abelian groups include Z, Q, R, C under addition; nonzero Q, R, C under mul-
tiplication; and fixed-size matrices with entries in any of those four sets under addition. The
set restriction is essential: omitting zero breaks additive closure, while including zero prevents a
nontrivial multiplicative group.

question.text:
2
Every element of a group G satisfies g = e. Which statement must hold?
(A) |G| = 2
(B) G is cyclic
(C) G is finite
(D) G is Abelian
(E) G has no proper nontrivial subgroup

solution.text:
−1 −1 −1
Every element is its own inverse. Thus ab = (ab) = b a = ba. Elementary Abelian
2-groups can be noncyclic and arbitrarily large, so the other assertions are not forced.

question.text:
Elements a, b of a group have orders two and three, respectively. How many group elements x
can satisfy ax = xb?
(A) 0
(B) 1
(C) 2
(D) 3
(E) It depends on the group.

solution.text:
2 2 2 2
If ax = xb, then a x = xb . Since a = e, cancellation of x gives b = e, contrary to b hav-
ing order three. This uses the orders of the elements without commuting any factors.

question.text:
2 2 2
If a group satisfies (ab) = a b for all a, b, which follows?
(A) The group is trivial
(B) The group is finite
(C) The group is abelian
(D) The group is cyclic
(E) Every element has order two

solution.text:
The identity is abab = aabb. Cancel a on the left and b on the right to obtain ba = ab for
arbitrary elements.

question.text:
Which of the following, with the indicated ordinary operation, is an infinite Abelian group?
(A) Nonzero rational numbers under addition
(B) Positive integers under multiplication
(C) All real 2 × 3 matrices under addition
(D) All real 2 × 2 matrices under multiplication
(E) Positive real numbers under addition

solution.text:
Rectangular real matrices add entrywise, with the zero matrix as identity and −A as in-
verse; addition is commutative and there are infinitely many matrices. The first set is not
closed under addition. Positive integers lack multiplicative inverses in that set, all square
matrices include singular ones, and positive reals under addition omit the identity zero.
